phase0E_destinationHashExecution.evidence: Every current path hashes locally after download: FileStation downloads to /tmp then hashes; SCP downloads then hashes; mount transport hashes the WSL-side read. The restricted SSH proof allowlists rsync but not sha256sum.
phase0E_destinationHashExecution.consequence: Phase 0E fails as written. Verifying 14,005 objects would mean streaming the whole population back, which is both slow and weaker proof - exactly what Phase 0E exists to prevent.

newFinding_keyVersionNotSelfDescribing.statement: A stored ciphertext object is NOT self-describing as to key version.
newFinding_keyVersionNotSelfDescribing.evidence: Blob layout is [12-byte nonce][16-byte authTag][ciphertext] (crypto.mjs:172-174). There is no version field in the object. keyVersion is recorded only in the ledger entry's encryption metadata (worker.mjs:139) or inferred from the key env var name (estate-api.mjs:42-44).
newFinding_keyVersionNotSelfDescribing.consequence: An object separated from its ledger entry has no recoverable key version. Replicating objects to a durable store WITHOUT also durably replicating the ledger produces bytes that survive and cannot be opened - the DURABLE_BUT_UNDECRYPTABLE failure state the key-custody invariant exists to prevent.
newFinding_keyVersionNotSelfDescribing.correctsIntegratorsOwnContract: Phase 5F as written says to derive key version by parsing the envelope. That is not possible. Phase 5F must read the ledger entry, and the ledger must therefore be inside the replicated, WORM-protected set - not merely alongside it.
newFinding_keyVersionNotSelfDescribing.alsoNote: No standalone envelope-parse function exists. Only decryptObject (crypto.mjs:181-192) validates structure, and it requires the key. Phase 5E needs a key-free structural validator that does not yet exist.
